goal.text: Access to order, stock, and contract data verified for every request (zero trust)

query.organization_type: medium-sized distributor with an order portal and an LLM-based ordering assistant

kpis.text: Requests authenticated and authorized per request (100%)
Privileged actions protected by multi-factor authentication (100%)

beliefs: No network location, including the office network, is trusted by default

ranked_patterns.relevance: Highest relevance: SKB-04/G2 is the same goal type (every access request verified) with near-identical KPIs (per-request authentication/authorization at 100%, MFA on privileged sessions at 100%), the same belief that no network location is trusted by default, and the same constraint banning shared accounts. Its tasks (authenticate against the identity provider, evaluate policy per request, step-up authentication), its resources (identity provider, policy decision point) and its documented conflict resolution (cache non-privileged read decisions, always re-verify privileged actions) transfer directly to G05 for the order portal, stock and contract data.

Second: SKB-03/G3 contributes the identity-verification-before-release constraint and the register-and-close-within-a-deadline mechanism, which is the natural template for G05-K3 (quarterly access reviews completed) and for protecting contract and personal data handled by the Data Protection Officer in the query scope.

Third: SKB-07/G2 shares the regulated medicine-handling domain of the query (pharmaceutical distribution to hospitals). It supplies the role-restriction pattern (only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines) and the record-at-the-event traceability pattern, which are adapted here as pharmacist-only privileged actions and as access evidence logging required by regulated distribution.

Fourth: SKB-01/G2 is the order-to-cash counterpart and supplies the data objects and actors in scope of G05 (customer price lists/contract data, order management module, Sales Administrator, Customer as Hospital Buyer) plus the change-control constraint on confirmed orders, which G05 enforces at the access layer.

elements.text: LLM ordering assistant requests verified under the named end user's delegated identity
elements.justification: The query organization adds an LLM-based ordering assistant that is not present in SKB-04; because the assistant issues requests to order, stock and contract data, the per-request verification principle of SKB-04/G2 must be decomposed into a sub-goal covering non-human requesters, respecting the no-shared-accounts constraint.

elements.text: Authenticate every request to the order portal and to the ordering assistant against the corporate identity provider
elements.justification: Direct adaptation of 'Authenticate each request against the identity provider' to the portal and assistant channels, which is the mechanism that produces the 100% per-request authentication KPI.

elements.text: Evaluate access policy per request (role, device, context, customer contract scope) before order, stock or contract data is released
elements.justification: Adapts 'Evaluate access policy per request (role, device, context)' and extends the policy scope to the contract and stock data objects named in G05.

elements.text: Cache policy decisions for 5 minutes for non-privileged read requests while re-verifying every privileged action
elements.justification: Reuses the conflict resolution recorded in SKB-04/G2 (per-request checks added latency to staff screens) so that portal responsiveness for hospital buyers does not reduce per-request authorization coverage.

elements.text: Require step-up multi-factor authentication for privileged actions (contract price changes, bulk data export, quarantine release, access rights changes)
elements.justification: Adapts 'Require step-up authentication for privileged actions' and enumerates the privileged actions specific to pharmaceutical distribution, serving the 100% MFA KPI.

elements.text: Verify the requester's identity and entitlement before releasing contract, price or personal data to a hospital buyer or an external party
elements.justification: Adapts the SKB-03 practice of verifying identity before any data release, applied to the contract and personal data flowing through the order portal.

elements.text: Review all user, service and assistant access rights per role every quarter and revoke rights that are no longer justified
elements.justification: Adapts the register-verify-close cycle of SKB-03/G3 into the recurring access review required by G05-K3.

elements.text: Record each access review and each revocation in the access review register and close it within the quarter
elements.justification: Adapts 'Register and verify each data subject request' plus the closure deadline, giving the evidence needed to report the review completion KPI.

elements.text: Issue the ordering assistant a short-lived credential bound to the named hospital buyer or sales administrator for each session, never a standing service identity
elements.justification: Extends per-request verification to the LLM assistant so that assistant traffic is authenticated and authorized as the delegating user, respecting the no-shared-accounts constraint.

elements.text: Log every verified request with user identity, assistant session, and the order, batch or contract record accessed
elements.justification: Adapts the record-at-the-event traceability of SKB-07/G2 ('Record batch and expiry at receipt') to access events, producing the audit evidence a regulated distributor needs.

elements.text: Identity provider with multi-factor authentication
elements.justification: Taken directly from SKB-04/G2 resources; it is the system that performs authentication and step-up for every request.

elements.text: Policy decision point for per-request authorization
elements.justification: Taken directly from SKB-04/G2 resources; it evaluates role, device and context policy for each portal and assistant request.

elements.text: Access review register
elements.justification: Adapted from the SKB-03 'Request register' to record quarterly review items and their closure.

elements.text: Order management module holding order, stock and contract data
elements.justification: Adapted from SKB-01 resources ('Order management module', 'Customer price list'); it is the protected system whose data G05 governs.

elements.text: Access event log
elements.justification: Adapted from the batch-record traceability resource logic of SKB-07/G2 to hold access evidence for regulated audits.

elements.text: IT Security Officer
elements.justification: Owner of per-request verification policy and of the identity provider in SKB-04/G2; same role is listed in the query scope.

elements.text: Hospital Buyer
elements.justification: Adapts the 'Branch Staff' / 'Customer' requester role to the external portal user whose every request must be authenticated and authorized.

elements.text: Sales Administrator
elements.justification: Taken from SKB-01/G2; the internal order-entry role whose requests to contract and order data are subject to per-request verification.

elements.text: Data Protection Officer
elements.justification: Taken from SKB-03/G3; accountable for lawful access to personal and contract data and for reviewing entitlements.

elements.text: Responsible Pharmacist
elements.justification: Adapts the 'Pharmacist in Charge' authority of SKB-07/G2; the only role allowed to perform pharmaceutical privileged actions, which require step-up MFA.

elements.text: Quality Assurance Officer
elements.justification: Adapted from the regulated-control oversight role in SKB-07/G2; validates that access reviews and access evidence satisfy GDP audit expectations.

elements.text: AI Product Owner
elements.justification: No retrieved pattern covers an LLM assistant; this query-specific role is accountable for the assistant's delegated-identity behaviour.

elements.text: No network location, including the office network, is trusted by default
elements.justification: Confirms the query belief and the SKB-04/G2 belief that implicit network trust is what allows compromised sessions to move laterally.

elements.text: Regulated pharmaceutical distribution requires traceable evidence of who accessed order, batch and contract records
elements.justification: Adapts the SKB-07 belief that regulation requires batch records, transposed to access records in the distribution context.

elements.text: The LLM ordering assistant is a requester like any other and is never implicitly trusted
elements.justification: Needed to apply the zero-trust belief consistently to the non-human channel introduced by this organization; not present in any retrieved pattern.

elements.text: Shared accounts are not permitted, for human users and for the ordering assistant
elements.justification: Confirms the query constraint and extends the SKB-04/G2 constraint to the assistant so that every request is attributable to a named identity.

elements.text: Identity is verified before any order, contract or personal data is released
elements.justification: Taken from the SKB-03/G3 constraint; prevents data release on unverified requests and underpins the 100% authorization KPI.

elements.text: Only the Responsible Pharmacist may authorize release of quarantined or recalled batch records, and only after step-up multi-factor authentication
elements.justification: Adapts 'Only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines' into an access-control constraint combined with the MFA requirement of G05-K2.

elements.text: A confirmed order may only be changed through a change request raised by a re-verified, authorized user
elements.justification: Adapts the SKB-01/G2 change-control constraint and enforces it at the access layer so order integrity is protected by per-request verification.

elements.text: Cached authorization decisions may not be used for privileged actions
elements.justification: Boundary condition of the SKB-04/G2 latency conflict resolution, ensuring the caching task cannot weaken the 100% MFA coverage of privileged actions.

output.rational_statement: G05 serves the parent goal G01 'Regulated order-to-delivery controlled and secure' by removing the implicit trust that lets a compromised session read or change order, stock and contract data: every request from the portal, from internal staff, or from the LLM ordering assistant is authenticated against the identity provider and authorized by a policy decision point using role, device, context and contract scope (G05-K1), privileged actions such as contract price changes, bulk export and quarantine release are re-verified with step-up multi-factor authentication and are never served from cached decisions (G05-K2), and quarterly reviews recorded in the access review register remove rights that are no longer justified before they can be abused (G05-K3). Binding the assistant to short-lived credentials of the named delegating user and logging each verified access keeps the no-shared-accounts constraint enforceable and produces the attributable evidence a regulated hospital supplier must present, so that the control and security half of G01 is demonstrable rather than assumed.
